messages:
tamika: Heads up — after upgrading to @redwood/inference-js@2.2.0 our Next.js Edge functions started throwing at cold start: "ReferenceError: initRuntime is not defined". Bundle size also went up ~480KB in source-map-explorer.

owen: Can you paste the import lines? Are you using `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'` or default import?

tamika: default import in a small utils file: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'`

harper: default + exported CJS can cause rollup/webpack to emit a commonjs interop wrapper that defeats tree-shaking. Did you inspect package.json in 2.2.0?

tamika: pasted relevant bits from node_modules:
```
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.js",
"sideEffects": false,
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./runtime": { "import": "./dist/esm/runtime.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/runtime.js" }
}
```

harper: yep — sideEffects:false hides the runtime file unless explicitly referenced. Our runtime file registers a tiny global polyfill and sets up default fetch; if bundlers drop it, the edge runtime lacks the init code -> ReferenceError.

owen: For app owners: quick fixes that worked for me in similar cases:
- switch to named imports from ESM entry: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js/esm'`
- or add the runtime path to your bundler's keep list (vite: build.rollupOptions.input or optimizeDeps.include/exclude hacks)
- pin to 2.1.x until upstream fixes

kevin: We should communicate this in the upgrade guide. Also upstream needs to either remove sideEffects:false or add "./dist/esm/runtime.js" to the sideEffects allowlist. Another option: move runtime boot into an explicit exported function (e.g., `initRuntime()`) so consumers opt-in.

tamika: I tried the named-ESM import — reduced size but breaks TypeScript resolution in our monorepo without extra path mappings. Not ideal for onboarding.

harper: Also watch out for published bundles that use Rollup's CJS interop helpers (createCommonjsModule). Those inline shims make ESM imports pull the entire CJS output. We should prefer a build that emits a clean ESM entry that directly exports the functions without re-exporting CJS default.

build-bot: CI note: created ticket DEVEX-5895. Repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-internal/rw-inference-repro/tree/esm-cjs-sideeffects

kevin: Action items for SDK maintainers:
1) revert/remove sideEffects flag or add runtime file to allowlist
2) publish a true ESM-first artifact (no CJS re-export shims)
3) include a `runtime` explicit export and document side-effects in README
4) add integration tests: vite/esbuild/webpack + node/edge + webpack5 tree-shaking

owen: For now we'll add a short troubleshooting checklist to the SDK upgrade doc and a note in the Next.js/Edge recipe. Also pushing a tiny sample app showing correct imports to the examples folder.

tamika: Thanks — pinning to 2.1.x and using the workaround in prod until a patch ships. Posting results in the FD slack channel in case customers hit this. :thumbsup:
